governance_note: The CAP-13-owned governed artifact of the planar single-force moment method, under STAGE25_CAP13_PLANAR_SINGLE_FORCE_MOMENT_METHOD_CONTRACT.md. It carries the method authority (identity, version, model, executed form and derivation), the applicability declarations, the numeric domain, the high-risk screen, the limitations, the fixed disclosure meaning and the source and source-use records. It is NOT a Domain Pack and NOT an entry in domains/domain_provenance.json; it is separate from the two-support static reactions artifact, never loads it and is never loaded by it. Calculation execution belongs to the shared deterministic calculation and units owner; nothing here is evidence, a specification, a capacity, strength, equilibrium, adequacy or safety statement, or a readiness, progression or validation input.

method.model: ONE declared force acting in ONE plane, and ONE point in that same plane chosen by the inventor; the magnitude of the moment (turning effect) of that one force about that one point, given the inventor's own force magnitude F and the inventor's own perpendicular distance d_perp from the point to the force's line of action.
method.executed_form: M = F * d_perp. One multiplication of the two typed inputs, accepted only when finite, strictly positive and within a relative error of 2^-52 of the exact product of the two binary input values; no tolerance widening, no rounding, no clamping and no magnitude ceiling.
method.derivation: The moment of a force about a point is the force multiplied by the perpendicular distance from the point to the force's line of action (NASA-S1, NASA-T1). With F in N and d_perp in mm the product is directly in N·mm; no conversion factor is applied. The magnitude form, the planar restriction and the declarations are InventorAI's own bounded restatement; NASA does not publish this method.

roles.meaning: magnitude of the one declared force
perpendicular distance from the inventor's chosen point to the line of action of the one force (the role written d-perp)
magnitude of the moment of that one force about that one point; never a sign, direction, resultant, capacity or limit

rules: F and d_perp are finite numbers strictly greater than zero; a string, boolean, NaN, infinity, zero, negative value or any other non-finite or non-numeric value is INVALID_NUMERIC_INPUT, resolved before the shared owner is called. A zero input is refused, never computed: a line of action through the point gives no moment to calculate here.
No physical magnitude ceiling exists, and none is part of the admitted engineering domain.

Numerical acceptance: the computed M is accepted only when it is finite, strictly positive and within a relative error of 2^-52 of the exact mathematical product of the two actual binary input values. A subnormal M is accepted when it meets that bound and is never refused merely for being subnormal.

An overflow, an underflow to zero or a result outside the accepted relative error from a finite admitted pair is FAILURE / EXECUTION_INTEGRITY_FAILURE with no numerical payload; it is never rewritten as a refusal.

Each typed numeric field is capped at 64 characters for abuse and resource protection only; that bound is NON-PHYSICAL, is NOT the admitted engineering domain and is never described as a range of valid forces or distances. Over-length text is INVALID_NUMERIC_INPUT.
Grammar: strict ASCII decimal digits with an optional single fractional part; no sign, exponent, separator, Unicode digit, unit suffix or normalization.

declarations.accepted_value: planar: the force and the chosen point lie in one plane, and only the turning effect about the axis through the point at right angles to that plane is wanted
ONE force only: no other force, couple, spread-out load or weight is included in this calculation

the distance d_perp is the shortest (perpendicular) distance from the chosen point to the line along which the force acts, not a length along a lever, arm or part unless that length is itself at right angles to the force; InventorAI does not check it
the point is the inventor's own choice (for example a pivot, joint or fixing); InventorAI does not choose it, check it or decide that it is the right point
the force is treated as steady (static), and only the size of the moment is wanted, not its turning direction; no motion, impact, vibration or repeated loading is considered

limitations: No static equilibrium, moment balance, resultant, support reaction or sign convention; no joint, fastener, shaft, bearing, weld or member capacity, strength, stress, deflection, fatigue or failure check; no torque rating, motor or actuator sizing; no thickness, material or specification; no design suitability, stability or safety conclusion; no inference of any declaration, force, distance or point.

Three-dimensional moments, several forces, couples, spread-out loads, friction, motion, impact, vibration and repeated loading are outside this calculation, and no conversion of N·mm to any other unit is performed.
All NO answers on the high-risk screen only allow this bounded calculation to proceed; they never mean safe. The screen neither reads nor feeds SafetySignal.
The result is UNVALIDATED and is not evidence; it is request-local and is not stored, reported, exported or used for readiness, progression or validation.
disclosure: This is the size of the turning effect (moment) of the one force you declared about the one point you chose, in one plane, using your own force F and your own perpendicular distance d⊥.
It does not show that anything is balanced or held in place, and it gives no support reaction, turning direction or combined effect of several forces.
It does not tell whether a joint, fixing, shaft, part, motor or material can carry this moment, and it is not compared with any rating, strength or limit.

It is preliminary, advisory, UNVALIDATED and not evidence, and it must be confirmed by measurement or a qualified engineer before any reliance; it says nothing about whether the design is suitable or safe.
InventorAI does not check your force, your distance, your chosen point or that your declarations match the real configuration.
Three-dimensional effects, several forces, motion, impact, vibration and repeated loading are outside this calculation.
Reference source material: NASA Glenn Research Center (equilibrium and torque / moment principles); the moment form is InventorAI's own restatement.
